'''Shigeoka Kawahito''' (滋岳川人) was a {{ill|Heian period|ar|فترة هييآن|ast|Periodu Heian|az|Heyan dövrü|bcl|Panahon ni Heian|bg|Хеян|bn|হেইআন যুগ|br|Marevezh Heian|ca|Període Heian|cs|Období Heian|de|Heian-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Χεϊάν|eo|Epoko Heian|es|Período Heian|eu|Heian aroa|fa|دوره هی‌آن|fi|Heian-kausi|fr|Époque de Heian|gl|Período Heian|he|תקופת הייאן|hi|हेआन काल|hr|Heian (razdoblje)|hu|Heian-kor|hy|Հեիան ժամանակաշրջան|id|Zaman Heian|it|Periodo Heian|ja|平安時代|ka|ჰეიანის პერიოდი|ko|헤이안 시대|la|Aevum Heian|lt|Hejano laikotarpis|mn|Хэйан|mr|हियन कालावधी|ms|Zaman Heian|my|ဟဲအိအန်ခေတ်|nl|Heianperiode|nn|Heian|no|Heian-perioden|oc|Epòca d'Heian|pl|Heian|ps|هېيان دوره|pt|Período Heian|ro|Perioada Heian|ru|Период Хэйан|sh|Heianski period|simple|Heian period|sk|Obdobie Heian|sl|Obdobje Heian|sq|Periudha Heian|sr|Хеиан период|sv|Heian|ta|ஹையன் காலகட்டம்|th|ยุคเฮอัง|tl|Panahong Heian|tr|Heian Dönemi|uk|Період Хейан|vi|Thời kỳ Heian|war|Panahon Heian|wuu|平安时代|zh|平安时代|zh_classical|平安朝|zh_min_nan|Heian sî-tāi|zh_yue|平安時代|qid=Q193292|lt=Heian period}} aristocrat and {{ill|Onmyōji|en|Onmyōji|qid=Q2274163|lt=Onmyōji}}. His family name transitioned from {{ill|Togi no Ason|ja|刀岐直}} to {{ill|Shigeoka no Ason|ja|滋岳朝臣}}. His court Rank reached {{ill|Junior Fifth Rank|ja|従五位上|lt=Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade}}, and he served as the {{ill|Yin-Yang Bureau|ja|陰陽頭|zh|阴阳头|qid=Q11658275}}.

== Lineage ==
The origins of the Togi clan (刀岐氏) are unclear, but they are thought to be descended from the {{ill|Mikata District, Hyōgo|en|Mikata District, Hyōgo|qid=Q1155035|lt=Mikata District}} Togi area in {{ill|Tajima Province|cs|Tadžima (provincie)|de|Provinz Tajima|es|Provincia de Tajima|fa|ولایت تاجیما|fr|Province de Tajima|gl|Provincia de Tajima|id|Provinsi Tajima|it|Tajima (provincia)|ja|但馬国|ko|다지마국|lt|Tadžimos žemė|nl|Tajima (provincie)|pt|Província de Tajima|ru|Тадзима (провинция)|simple|Tajima Province|sk|Tadžima (provincia)|sr|Провинција Таџима|tr|Tajima (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Тадзіма|zh|但馬國|zh_min_nan|Tazima-kok|qid=Q1053727|lt=Tajima Province}} (modern {{ill|Shin'onsen, Hyōgo|en|Shin'onsen, Hyōgo|qid=Q1154955|lt=Shin'onsen Town}}, {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|en|Hyōgo Prefecture|qid=Q130290|lt=Hyōgo Prefecture}}){{sfn|Ōta|1963|loc=3908}}. As a clan with the "Na" surname (直), they may have also been part of the {{ill|Futakata Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|二方国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mikata Province Governors|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q108487217}} lineage.

== Career ==
In {{ill|Ninju 4|ja|仁寿4年}} ({{ill|854|en|854|qid=Q24981|lt=854}}), Kawahito and his relatives, including Togi no Masaru (then serving as {{ill|Kazusa Province|en|Kazusa Province|qid=Q1055394|lt=Kazusa Province}} Provincial Secretary), were granted the surname {{ill|Shigeoka no Ason|ja|滋岳朝臣}}. At the time, he held the Rank {{ill|Senior Sixth Rank|ja|正六位上|lt=Senior Sixth Rank, Upper Grade}} and the positions {{ill|Junior Assistant of the Bureau of Onmyō|ja|陰陽権允}} and {{ill|Onmyō Hakase|ja|陰陽博士}}. Kawahito continued to serve as an Onmyō Doctor for more than 20 years, spanning the reigns of {{ill|Emperor Montoku|ar|الإمبراطور مونتوكو|azb|مونتوکو (ایمپیراتور)|be|Імператар Мантоку|ca|Montoku Tennō|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر مۆنتۆکو|cs|Montoku|de|Montoku|es|Montoku Tennō|eu|Montoku enperadorea|fa|امپراتور مونتوکو|fr|Montoku (empereur)|he|מונטוקו|id|Montoku|it|Montoku|ja|文徳天皇|ko|몬토쿠 천황|nl|Montoku|pl|Montoku|pt|Montoku|ru|Император Монтоку|sh|Car Montoku|simple|Emperor Montoku|sl|Cesar Montoku|sv|Kejsar Montoku|sw|Montoku wa Japani|th|จักรพรรดิมนโตกุ|tl|Emperador Montoku|tr|Montoku (imparator)|uk|Імператор Монтоку|vi|Thiên hoàng Montoku|yo|Emperor Montoku|zh|文德天皇|zh_min_nan|Montoku Thian-hông|qid=Q357225|lt=Emperor Montoku}} and {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa}}, eventually ascending to {{ill|Yin-Yang Bureau|ja|陰陽頭|zh|阴阳头|qid=Q11658275}}. As an Onmyōji, his activities are well documented:
- In {{ill|Tian'an 2|ja|天安2年}} ({{ill|858|en|858|qid=Q30371|lt=858}}), Kawahito, along with {{ill|Abe no Yasuhito|ja|安倍安仁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe no Asomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11450312}} and others, selected a burial site for {{ill|Emperor Montoku|ar|الإمبراطور مونتوكو|azb|مونتوکو (ایمپیراتور)|be|Імператар Мантоку|ca|Montoku Tennō|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر مۆنتۆکو|cs|Montoku|de|Montoku|es|Montoku Tennō|eu|Montoku enperadorea|fa|امپراتور مونتوکو|fr|Montoku (empereur)|he|מונטוקו|id|Montoku|it|Montoku|ja|文徳天皇|ko|몬토쿠 천황|nl|Montoku|pl|Montoku|pt|Montoku|ru|Император Монтоку|sh|Car Montoku|simple|Emperor Montoku|sl|Cesar Montoku|sv|Kejsar Montoku|sw|Montoku wa Japani|th|จักรพรรดิมนโตกุ|tl|Emperador Montoku|tr|Montoku (imparator)|uk|Імператор Монтоку|vi|Thiên hoàng Montoku|yo|Emperor Montoku|zh|文德天皇|zh_min_nan|Montoku Thian-hông|qid=Q357225|lt=Emperor Montoku}} in the {{ill|Kadono district|ja|葛野郡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katsuno District|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q13579879}}, {{ill|Yamashiro Province|ja|Yamashiro Province}}.<ref>『{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qid=Q1052981|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}』天安2nd year 9月2日条</ref>
- In {{ill|Jōgan 1|ja|貞観元年}} ({{ill|859|en|859|qid=Q23897|lt=859}}), he and {{ill|Fujiwara no Yamakage|ja|藤原山蔭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujihara no Yamakage|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11623214}} performed a ritual in {{ill|Yoshino District, Nara|en|Yoshino District, Nara|qid=Q1154558|lt=Yoshino District}}, {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|qid=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province}} to prevent pestilence.<ref>『{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qid=Q1052981|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}』貞観元年8月3日条</ref>
- In {{ill|Jōgan 5|ja|貞観5年}} ({{ill|863|en|863|qid=Q25052|lt=863}}), he conducted further rituals to address similar concerns.<ref>『日本三代実録』貞観5th year 2月1日条</ref>
Kawahito's activities significantly influenced the rituals and practices during this period, particularly in the establishment of the {{ill|Takayama Festival|en|Takayama Festival|qid=Q7677467|lt=Takamayama Festival}}.

== Works and Legacy ==
Kawahito is credited with foundational works in Japanese {{ill|Onmyōdō|en|Onmyōdō|qid=Q1340540|lt=Onmyōdō}}, including 『{{ill|Seiyō Dōsei-kyō|ja|世要動静経}}』 and 『{{ill|Kinshū Shinjutsu Tonkō-sho|ja|滋川新術遁甲書}}』.<ref>{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qid=Q1052981|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}貞観16年5月27日条</ref> Although these are lost, they heavily influenced subsequent practitioners and texts.
